tasks.short: Secure required event permits for displays, exhibits, and food service.

steps.what: Gather event details, venue plans, display specifications, and food service arrangements.
Find official application forms, requirements, fees, and submission deadlines.
Confirm responsibilities and applicable permissions with venue staff and relevant authorities.
Request missing plans, certificates, and declarations from venue staff and suppliers.
Complete application forms and assemble supporting evidence.
Check safety evidence, factual declarations, responsibilities, and fees before approving submission.
Submit the approved application through the required official channel.
Resolve authority questions and coordinate any required inspection or application changes.
Review the authority's decision and record conditions, deadlines, and required operating changes.

loop.input: Authority decision and attached permit conditions.
loop.output: Draft condition register with source passages, dates, restrictions, and unresolved ambiguities.
loop.check: Validate dates and required fields; planner compares every condition with the original decision.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per decision; unreadable or ambiguous text returns to the planner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Conditions arrive in varied free text; fixed fields cannot reliably capture their wording and exceptions.

steps.what: Send confirmed restrictions to responsible teams and schedule checks before the event.

tasks.design: Configure a permit register in {WORKFLOW}, linked to event records in {PROJECT} and evidence in {DOCS}, with official {GOV_PORTAL} links, supplier reminders through {EMAIL}, and deterministic application generation. Keep applicability discussions, safety approval, and portal submission with people; a bounded extraction loop drafts permit conditions for review before {WORKFLOW} assigns checks and sends approved instructions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements differ by authority, venue, activity, and existing permissions. Infrequent applications rarely justified bespoke integrations, while evidence collection crossed several organisations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, document templates, and workflow configuration cover much of the administration. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and generating applications; bounded extraction can help with varied decision letters.
tasks.still_hard: Confirming which permissions actually apply, assessing technical evidence, and negotiating changes remain demanding. Authority portals may lack interfaces, and inspections depend on external availability.
tasks.human_edge: The planner resolves unclear responsibilities and coordinates practical changes with venue staff, suppliers, and authorities. Competent people remain responsible for safety judgements and declarations.

ambition.what: Early permit readiness checks for small events before venue commitments.

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling forms and chasing attachments, and more time resolving venue constraints early. With delegated authority, they can request missing evidence and flag booking holds; safety approval and authority decisions retain their existing owners.

reach.task: Assess event feasibility before approving venue commitments.
reach.learn: Budget approval stages, booking cancellation terms, and how permit lead times affect campaign timing.

reach.task: Evaluate event catering and temporary display arrangements.
reach.learn: How material, waste, and catering choices affect both practical permissions and sustainability requirements.

evidence.claim: Configured checklists, reminders, document generation, and evidence registers can reduce permit administration; the digest supplies no event-permit-specific case.
Venue permissions and responsibility for food service or temporary structures must be checked against applicable local and national rules.
The time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured results.
GDPR applies to personal data in applications; consultation requirements depend on national rules and the actual employee-data processing introduced.

assumptions: This is an occasional task in a mid-size European marketing team; venue staff and suppliers provide technical evidence.
Some events use existing venue permissions, so the checklist can close an application path when coverage is confirmed.
Configured official links support retrieval; a person checks current requirements for each unfamiliar authority or event type.
Application generation uses verified fields and attachments, without automatically asserting legal compliance.
The submission channel is represented by {GOV_PORTAL}; some authorities instead require email or paper.
Time shares represent active work, excluding authority processing delays.
Material application amendments repeat the approval step before submission.
Automatic requests and instructions use approved recipients, templates, and confirmed records.
Access estimates include privacy review and any required employee consultation under national rules; they exclude authority permit lead times.
The bounded extraction supports document handling; it does not evaluate workers or make permit decisions.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, venues, event types, and annual application volumes the team handles.
Which permissions the venues and caterers already hold.
Who can approve declarations, fees, application amendments, and booking holds.
Whether existing {WORKFLOW}, {PROJECT}, and {DOCS} access supports configuration and integration.
Which authority channels the team actually uses.
Whether proposed data handling triggers employee consultation under applicable national rules.
How much current effort goes into repeat applications versus unfamiliar cases.
research_questions: Which official authority handles each activity, and what are its current forms, deadlines, and evidence requirements?
When do existing venue or supplier permissions cover the planned activity?
Which official channels support reusable forms, electronic submissions, or status notifications?
What national rules govern temporary displays, fire safety, food service, and relevant employee consultation?
new_work: Maintain official links, form versions, evidence checklists, and reminder schedules.
Review extracted conditions against original decisions and resolve ambiguous wording.
Handle incomplete supplier evidence and unusual venue requirements.
Check that application changes receive renewed approval when needed.
Maintain access permissions, retention periods, and integration failures.

role.altitude: The event planner becomes an earlier adviser on event feasibility, with less document assembly and chasing. Formal safety, spending, and permit decision rights change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Help marketing managers assess permit constraints before venue commitments.
Work with sustainability specialists on feasible catering and display choices.
skills_to_grow: Interpreting official requirements and recognising when specialist advice is needed.
Structured evidence collection and workflow configuration.
Reviewing extracted conditions against source documents.
Assessing venue feasibility and escalation timing.
role.ambitious_version: Offer an early permit readiness service that helps smaller event organisers choose feasible venues and activities before committing funds.
